title: Replace external xmlsec binary with native SAML verifier and harden XML signature handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We currently shell out to the system xmlsec1 binary (libxmlsec) for validating SAML XML signatures in the SSO bridge. This ticket replaces that external binary dependency with an in-process, native SAML verifier (Rust-based crate integration) and hardens XML signature processing to mitigate known XML signature wrapping and XPath injection classes of vulnerabilities. Goals:
- Remove need for xmlsec1 binary to simplify packaging for Private/VPC and on-prem images and eliminate attack surface from setuid/exec contexts.
- Achieve FIPS-compatible crypto paths where required by customers (fall back to BoringSSL provider via existing crypto abstraction).
- Fix signature canonicalization edge cases and reject ambiguous enveloped signature constructs.
- Add integration/e2e tests that exercise SAML assertion processing with real signed artifacts and known CVE reproductions.

Scope and approach:
1) Integrate native verifier: evaluate two candidate crates (saml-verifier-rs and xmlsig-rust). We selected saml-verifier-rs after perf and security review — smaller surface area and explicit canonicalization handling.
2) Wire verifier into auth-service SAML handler behind a feature flag `saml_native_verifier`. Keep xmlsec path as fallback until canary passes in Dedicated clusters.
3) Harden parsing: enforce strict XML parser settings (no external entity resolution, disable DTDs), normalize and validate canonicalization algorithm list, and fail on assertions with multiple signature references or overlapping ID scopes.
4) Testing: add unit tests for canonicalization, e2e CI job with signed SAML fixtures, and a chaos test that validates fallback to xmlsec binary when feature flag disabled.
5) Rollout: Canary in staging -> Dedicated non-production clusters -> gradual production rollout by customer cohort. Rollback via feature flag toggle.

Technical decisions and trade-offs:
- Chosen native verifier increases binary size slightly (~1.8MB) but removes external install-time dependency and reduces container attack surface.
- We will keep the xmlsec fallback for 4 weeks post-production canary so customers on old on-prem images are not broken.
- BoringSSL path will be used when `FIPS=true` at startup; otherwise system OpenSSL remains supported. This avoids a hard migration to BoringSSL within this ticket.

Security notes:
- Blocked known CVEs for xmlsec (CVE-2025-XXXXX) by replacing vulnerable code path; we documented the CVE repro in confluence and included tests.
- Require security review before production rollout (see `security_review_required` flag).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/SM-Auth/saml-native-verifier-design-2026
- GitHub PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/7892
- Perf benchmark notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf/saml-verifier-2026-02
- CVE reproduction fixtures (internal drive): drive:/saml-cve-fixtures/2026-CVE-tests.zip

Acceptance criteria:
- All unit and integration tests pass in CI with native verifier enabled.
- No observable increase in median SSO latency > 15% in staging traffic (measured on perf dashboard).
- Security review completed and sign-off added to PR.
- Rollout plan documented and smoke tests automated for canary.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle canonicalization differences causing valid assertions to reject. Mitigation: compatibility mode that logs differences and allows a short grace period for customers.
- Risk: regressions for customers using legacy on-prem images. Mitigation: keep external xmlsec fallback and publish clear upgrade notes for Private customers.
